objective: Apply the length-tension relationship (peak tension at about 80 to 120 percent of a sarcomere's resting length) to explain why a muscle is weaker when much shorter or much longer than that
secondaryObjectives: Explain how endurance training, resistance training and disuse change muscle: mitochondria and capillaries, hypertrophy and atrophy

sources.cite: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e (Oregon State University edition), 10.4 Nervous System Control of Muscle Tension
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. 'The ideal length of a sarcomere to produce maximal tension occurs at 80 percent to 120 percent of its resting length'; stretched beyond that the filaments do not fully overlap, and shortened below it the zone of overlap is reduced, so tension drops either way.

brief.situation: You help maintain the outcomes dashboard at Cedar Valley Outpatient Rehab (fictional) as a rehab aide with data duties. Average quadriceps strength at discharge fell 25% this month. A new dynamometer setup began the same week. The quality report goes at 16:00. It is 15:05. All records are invented teaching data.
handover: Old protocol: knee extension measured with the knee at 60 degrees of flexion.
New setup sheet: knee at 10 degrees of flexion, near full extension, where the quadriceps is short.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the coordinator: why strength appeared to fall, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Force depends on muscle length: peak tension near 80 to 120% of resting sarcomere length. Near full knee extension the quadriceps is short, overlap is reduced, and peak torque is lower.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Compare only results at the same angle and restore the 60-degree setup; a scale factor or blaming the program misreads a measurement change.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: 60-degree results match last month; paired tests show the angle effect.

scoring.modelReasoning: A drop that starts the week the test position changed points at the measurement. At 10 degrees of knee flexion the quadriceps is short, below the 80 to 120% range where sarcomere overlap gives peak tension, so it produces less force. Results at 60 degrees match last month, and patients tested both ways are lower at 10 degrees. Report like-for-like results and restore the 60-degree setup; a scale factor guesses, and blaming the program is wrong.
